title: Restricted Right-Sided Initial-Derivative Bootstrap Characterization
question: For the existing SWAP mixed-form Richards owner in a strictly unsaturated restricted envelope, does a right-sided semi-discrete derivative constructed from current capacity and the new-boundary residual converge to the observed initial slope of accepted backward-Euler trajectories as dt decreases?
structural_pass_conditions: all declared capacities are finite and strictly positive
all declared direct backward-Euler trajectories converge under unchanged F-VQ29 numerical controls
hard external mass residual <= 1e-12 for every direct trajectory
finite-difference initial-slope error decreases strictly over the frozen decreasing-dt sequence for every case
smallest-dt slope error is less than the largest-dt slope error for every case
bootstrap derivative and smallest-dt observed slope have matching sign at the directly stimulated boundary node when nonzero
O0 and O2 textual outputs are identical
not_tested_or_not_claimed: root uptake or other source/sink dynamics
failure_interpretation: Any failure leaves the right-sided bootstrap unqualified and does not authorize tolerance, iteration-budget, dt-grid, state-matrix or physics changes after observing results.
success_interpretation: A pass only qualifies the restricted derivative-bootstrap construction as a test-supported owner operation. It unlocks, but does not itself qualify, a later test-only temporal-observer gate.
